subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What different kinds of hardware problems appear in these incidents?

judge.implied_focus: Characterization/taxonomy of hardware failures in incidents (how hardware problems manifest, what they affect, and why they fail)

per_column.name: problem_manifestation
per_column.rationale: Captures the observable symptom of the hardware problem (connectivity, not powering on, error message), a core facet of characterizing hardware issues.

per_column.name: affected_scope
per_column.rationale: Captures what the hardware problem affects (infrastructure vs single-user device vs shared equipment), an impact facet consistent with the same hardware-problem focus.

per_column.name: failure_mechanism
per_column.rationale: Captures the underlying cause/mode of failure (component, power, boot, connectivity), a causal facet distinct from manifestation, deepening the same focus.

judge.rationale: All three columns centre coherently on a single inferable focus: the nature of hardware problems in these incidents. They form a sound multi-facet structure (symptom/manifestation, impact/scope, root cause/mechanism) rather than a restatement or noise, and each is at a useful categorical granularity. Manifestation and failure_mechanism overlap somewhat (connectivity_issue vs connectivity_failure), slightly blurring the symptom/cause distinction, but they remain distinguishable enough to add analytical value. The focus is actionable: an analyst could triage, prioritize, and target remediation by manifestation, scope, and mechanism. High NULL counts (especially failure_mechanism) are a data-coverage concern but do not undermine the conceptual coherence or actionability of the proposed focus.
